# The module platform

The part of the core every module stage stands on: where a module plugs in, how a workspace switches one off, what the core says while one is off, and the AI tools’ server that a module’s tools answer through. **Stage 3 builds it** ([stage 3](stage-3-core-screens.md), “What to build”), empty of modules: a core with no module installed still has every place, Workspace → Features (with no switch on it), and a server answering the core’s own tools. Each module stage then only registers into it; its entry criteria point here.

It is written from Faro’s code: the places from `PLACES` in `src/core/module.ts`, the switch’s rule from `resolveModules` there and `setModule` in `src/domain/actions.ts`, every sentence from the function or file that says it, and the server from `src/mcp/protocol.ts` and `server/mcp.ts` (`src/spec/modulePlatform.ts`; its test fails when one of them changes and this page doesn’t).

## A module, as the core sees it

A module is a folder with its facts as plain data (Faro’s `module.json`, typed `ModuleFacts` in `src/core/module.ts`) and, optionally, its screens, Help, AI tools, records, actions and rules. The core never names a module: it reads the installed modules’ facts and asks each what it adds. A build can leave a module out altogether (Faro’s `FARO_WITHOUT=<id>`): then it is simply not there, and nothing of it is read or written.

| Fact | What it is |
|---|---|
| `id` | Lower case, words joined by hyphens. Never changes: a workspace switches a module off by it. |
| `name`, `summary` | What Workspace → Features shows: its name and one sentence of what it lets people do. `name` is also `{Module}` in every sentence below. |
| `group` | Its group on Features: `together` (Working together), `tools` (Tools), `beyond` (Beyond this workspace); `tools` when it says none. |
| `needs` | The modules it can’t work without. It is off whenever one of them is off or left out. |
| `routes`, `redirects` | Its pages (each with a Help article), and old addresses that lead to one of them. |
| `navigation`, `menu.waitsFor` | Its menu rows, each in a group (`work`, after Reviews; `lookup`, the default, after People and before Activity and Data; also under More on a phone); a row can wait until the module has a first record. |
| `places` | The places on core screens it fills (below). |
| `sections` | Workspace sections it adds: each at `/workspace/<id>`, in Workspace’s menu after the section it names, with a Help article; admins only when it says so. |
| `finders`, `filters`, `toSortOut` | Kinds of thing it makes findable (find-and-pick and Find, through the `Search` port), filters it adds to Goals (declared as data: a column compared with what is picked), and things to sort out on Workspace’s About without a section of its own. |
| `tables`, `records` | Its own records, which the core stores without knowing what they are (stage 2: rows each way, filed under `modules[<id>][<key>]`, saved in the same save as the core’s records, all or nothing). |
| `aiTools`, `help` | Its AI tools, offered by the core’s server, and its Help articles, merged into the core’s Help after the article each names. |
| `requirements`, `journeys` | What proves it: left out of the core’s journeys when the module is left out. |

## Where a module plugs in

A place is a spot on a core screen that draws whatever the modules that are on put there, in module order (their ids, A to Z), and nothing at all when none does. Build every place empty in stage 3; a screen renders it as one call (Faro: `<Place name="…" … />`).

| Place | Where the core draws it | What a module’s part is given |
|---|---|---|
| `home.blocks` | Home, after its own blocks (after “Goals you watch”) | nothing |
| `goal.facts` | A goal’s summary: one short line under its owner and level (“Measured by …”) | the goal |
| `goal.sections` | A goal’s page, inside About this goal, after its facts | the goal |
| `data.tools` | Data’s toolbar, after Columns and Saved layouts | the open table’s name, and the table exactly as laid out |
| `goals.tools` | Goals’ Views menu (the View sheet on a phone), after Copy link | the goals shown now and the view’s name |
| `goal.measure` | New goal (after “How it’s measured”) and Change a goal (after the name and, for a goal with a number, its “What it measures”): the “Measured by” field | the goal as saved (none while new), the form’s kind, unit, decimals and team, and `onChange(pick)`: one of the module’s actions and its input, which the form runs after the goal |
| `people.person` | A person’s page in People, after their facts | the person |
| `people.team` | A team’s page in People, after its people | the team |
| `help.article` | A Help article, under its title, before its sections | the article’s id, so a module draws only in its own article |
| `checkin.number` | The check-in, under the number field | the goal and week, the field’s value and `setValue`, last week’s number, what the latest check-in recorded of a source, and `onReading` (the reading to post, which the check-in’s rule checks again) |
| `checkin.table` | The one-table check-in, under the table | the table’s goals, and `onReadings` (fresh readings by goal) |
| `review.row` | A review’s agenda, one quiet line under a goal’s row | the goal (read-only: nothing in a review changes what measures it) |

Every part is also given who is looking (the viewer), the workspace and which modules are on: Faro’s parts read them from the app’s state, so the table names only what is particular to the place; a rebuild that draws on the server passes them in. Watch and Watched by, “Owners don’t need to watch…”, Make an MCP token (for admins), a review’s walk and Wrap up this goal all turn on who is looking.

Beside the places, a module may add:

- **Routes**: its pages, each with a name from its thing for the top bar and the browser’s title (rule 2 of [navigation](../core/rules/navigation.md)); a page marked focused takes the screen without the menu, as a check-in does. An address of a module that is off is Page not found, with the module’s sentence (below). A route may hold a parameter (`/metrics/:metricId`, `/reviews/:reviewId`, `/retro/:goalId`, `/data/import/done/:importId`), take a form or a file sent to it (Spreadsheets’ upload; every module’s form goes through the one dispatcher), answer with a download (the workbook and CSV files) or a redirect, and bring the module’s own script and styles, loaded only on its pages. A module’s `redirects` (old addresses, such as `/inbox` → `/feedback`) lead there while it is on and are Page not found while it is off.
- **Reads its pages fetch** (a JSON door): Feedback’s inbox reads its markups and feedback from its own store, not the workspace (Faro: the database’s functions; a rebuild: a read its server answers). While the module is off, the door answers with the page’s sentence.
- **Prompts** for the AI tools’ server, listed by `prompts/list` with the core’s (Feedback’s `review_inbox`), on or off.
- **Menu rows** in a group, placed by the menu rule ([navigation](../core/rules/navigation.md), the rows of `navigation.csv` with `example`), lit on its own pages.
- **Workspace sections**, **finders**, **Goals filters** and **things to sort out**, as in the table above.
- **Help articles**, each with the article it follows. They are the module’s own: [the Help guide](../core/help-guide.md) files each as “`{id}`, from the {module} module.”, and Help, Find and get_help leave every such article out while the module is off or left out of the build (a link to one says the module’s sentence). A module’s article with a core article’s id replaces it and leaves with the module.
- **AI tools**, listed by the server with the core’s (below).
- **Actions**, run by the one dispatcher like the core’s ([actions](../core/actions.md)): refused while the module is off. **Which sentence refuses them is the module’s choice** (a rebuild’s `offWords`): the long one, “{Module} is switched off in {workspace}. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, under Features.” (the default), or the short one, “{Module} is off in {workspace}.” (Watching’s Watch and Stop watching, the Wrap-up’s save, Feedback’s send and AI access’s make a token say the short one). **An action that only takes something away may run while its module is off** (a rebuild’s `whileOff`): revoking an AI token never refuses, so a token can be stopped while AI access is off; starting the next year is the core’s and never asks.
- **Its log entries’ shape**: an action’s change names its own thing (`entity: watch`, `review`, `field`, `metric`) and the goal it is about, so History reads it by goal; an action that changes nothing logs nothing.
- **Records** in the same save as the core’s (stage 2), and what the core’s own records need in that save when the module is switched off or on (the metric library lets go of the goals it held to no number, and holds them again).
- **A reader for a core AI tool’s part** (post_check_in’s `reading_confirmed` and `different_because` ask the metric library’s reader): with the module off, the tool says the module’s sentence.

**A Home card is not required.** `home.blocks` is a place like any other: a module that has something for Home draws it there, and while it is off nothing is drawn. Today Metric library draws one.; “no Home card” in a module’s switched-off criteria means none of its own, where it has one. Reviews’, Watching’s and the Wrap-up’s leads on Home are still the core’s, asking whether the module is on.

| `goalRhythm` | whenever what measures a goal changes: linked, unlinked, its refresh changed, the module switched | The goal’s own field `checkInRhythm` (monthly or quarterly; empty is the cycle’s), which the core’s due, run, habit and “No recent update” rules read (`domain/goalRhythm`). | `personLeft` | in the save that marks someone as left, or in which they leave | What the module passes from them to their lead: the core names the lead (their team’s lead; whoever takes over the team when they led it; else whoever marks them as left) and the module moves its own rows. To run the core’s journeys with a module off or left out, a build starts with modules switched off or not built (Faro: `FARO_MODULES_OFF=<ids|all>` and `FARO_WITHOUT=<ids>`); a core journey’s lines under “If the {module} module is on” are left out then ([how to read a journey](../core/journeys.md#how-to-read-a-journeys-steps)).

### What each installed module plugs in

Each one’s facts in full, as data, are in [`modules.json`](modules.json): every installed module’s `module.json` (its summary, routes, menu rows, places, sections, AI tools, Help articles, requirements and journeys), without its stage’s words, which are its stage page. A rebuild’s platform can load it as it is.

| Module | Summary (Features) | Group | Needs | Menu rows | Routes | Places | Workspace sections | Records | AI tools |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AI access (`ai-access`) | Let Claude or another AI tool read and act here through MCP, as one person, with that person’s rights. | beyond | — | — | 0 | — | `ai` | — | 3 |
| Feedback (`feedback`) | Send feedback about Faro, or mark up a screen. It goes to the people who build Faro. | beyond | — | — | 1 | — | — | — | 8 |
| Goal map (`goal-map`) | See every goal and what feeds it on one canvas, with the path the risk runs along. | tools | — | — | 0 | — | — | — | 0 |
| Metric library (`metrics`) | Define each number goals are measured by once (its meaning and calculation, unit, direction, source and owner), and say which metric measures a goal, for a team or the whole company. | tools | — | Metrics | 7 | `home.blocks`, `goal.facts`, `goal.measure`, `goal.sections`, `review.row`, `people.person`, `people.team`, `checkin.number`, `checkin.table` | — | metric, metric link | 9 |
| Reviews (`reviews`) | Walk a set of goals together on a cadence, decide what happens next and keep what was said. | together | — | — | 7 | — | — | — | 7 |
| Spreadsheets (`spreadsheets`) | Download the goals as an Excel workbook or CSV files, and load changes back from a spreadsheet, with every change shown before it’s saved. | tools | — | — | 5 | `data.tools`, `goals.tools`, `help.article` | — | — | 2 |
| Fields (`tags`) | Give goals a workspace’s own fields, such as a stage or a programme, to find and sort them by. | tools | — | — | 0 | `goal.sections` | `fields` | field, field value | 3 |
| Watching (`watching`) | Follow goals you don’t own: they show on your Home and under Watching in Goals. | together | — | — | 1 | — | — | — | 3 |
| Wrap-up (`wrap-up`) | At the end of the year, each owner says how their goals landed and what they learned. | together | — | — | 2 | — | — | — | 2 |

Several modules are switches whose screens are still the core’s (Reviews, Watching, the Wrap-up, the Goal map, Feedback, AI access): their pages, rows and leads are drawn by core screens that ask whether the module is on, so their `places` are empty. A rebuild may build them either way; what each must do while off is the same.

## Switching a module per workspace

- **The record.** `Workspace.modulesOff`: the ids an admin has switched off ([the data model](../core/data-model.md)). Empty or missing means every installed module is on. Stage 2 stores it with the workspace; nothing else holds the switch.
- **The rule.** A module is on when it is installed, not in `modulesOff`, and everything in its `needs` is on, however deep (`resolveModules`): switching one off switches off what needs it. Features says “Off until {the modules it needs} is on.” under such a module.
- **Who.** Admins only (“Only admins can switch features on or off.”), from Workspace → Features or the `set_feature` AI tool; an unknown id is refused (“There’s no feature called {id}.”). Switching to what it already is saves nothing.
- **The log.** One change on the workspace, `Switched off {Module}` (or `Switched on`), with “, and with it {the modules that need it}” when others go with it, and the diff `{Module}: On → Off`; with it, in the same save, whatever the module’s records say the core’s own records need.
- **While it is off:** no route (its addresses are Page not found, with its sentence), no menu row, nothing in any place, no Workspace section, no Help article (a link to one says its sentence), no walkthrough or named flow; its actions are refused and its AI tools answer with its sentence. What’s new still lists its releases. **Nothing it saved is deleted**: switched back on, everything is as it was.

## Workspace → Features

At `/workspace/features`, a Workspace section for admins (anyone else opening it is told who the admins are, with a way back). Its Help article is “Features” (`features`, [the Help guide](../core/help-guide.md)).

- First “How you work”, holding settings and no switch (the check-in rhythm, with Change). Then a group per “Working together”, “Tools”, “Beyond this workspace”, in that order, each listing its installed modules; a group with none is not drawn.
- Each module is one row: its name, its summary, a third line when it has something to say (its words are `features.line`’s, above), and a switch, a tick box named after the module, with its state in a word beside it (On or Off), never its position alone.
- Turning a switch acts at once, except for a module that owns something to keep: Reviews, Watching (with a watch kept), the Wrap-up (with a wrap-up written, or while it is open) and AI access (with a live token; both ways) first show a read-back of what leaves and what stays (`src/domain/switchOff.ts`, `reviewsOff.ts`; their words are in each module’s section), whose main button switches it.
- After a switch, the message with Undo (below); Undo switches it back and says “{Module} is off again.” or “{Module} is back on.”
- Under the groups: “Switching one off hides it and keeps what it saved.”, with links to Privacy and to the Help article.

## What the core says while a module is off

There are several sentences, each for one door; the stage pages quote them, and this is the list. `{Module}` is the module’s `name`, `{workspace}` the workspace’s name, `{tool}` the AI tool called.

| Where | The words | Said by |
|---|---|---|
| A page of a switched-off module: its address (Page not found) and its Help article, under the heading | “{Module} is switched off in {workspace}. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, Features.” | `src/ui/SwitchedOff.tsx` |
| An action of a switched-off module, refused by the app’s `run` (the AI tools don’t go through it: they say the tool’s sentence, below); also a save that writes Reviews’ records while Reviews is off | “{Module} is switched off in {workspace}. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, under Features.” | `switchedOffWords` (src/app/reads.ts) |
| One of the core’s own actions that belongs to a switch whose code is still the core’s (send feedback, write a wrap-up, make a token), refused; also Watch and Stop watching while Watching is off | “{Module} is off in {workspace}.” | `moduleOffWords` (src/app/reads.ts) |
| An AI tool of a switched-off module, called (`callTool`); the tool still shows in `tools/list`. Also a core tool asked for what a switched-off module adds: find_goals with a module’s filter, post_check_in with `reading_confirmed` or `different_because`, and bulk_change writing Reviews’ records or watches | “{Module} is switched off in {workspace}, so {tool} can’t be used there. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, under Features.” | `moduleOffSentence` (src/mcp/moduleOff.ts) |
| get_help asked for a switched-off module’s article | “{Module} is switched off in {workspace}, so its Help isn’t shown there. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, under Features.” | `src/mcp/workTools.ts` |
| Every request to the AI tools’ server but `initialize`, `tools/list` and notifications, while AI access is off (the door) | “AI access is switched off in {workspace}. An admin can switch it on in Faro, under Workspace, Features.” | `aiAccessShutWords` (src/app/reads.ts) |
| set_feature switching AI access off: the last thing that connection does | “AI access is off in {workspace}. This connection stops working now. An admin switches it back on in Faro.” | `aiAccessLastWords` (src/app/reads.ts) |
| The import’s file line, once, when Reviews is off and the file has Reviews’ sheet or column | “Reviews is off in {workspace}, so the Notes sheet and the Review column were not read.” | `reviewsOffReadLine` (src/domain/sheets.ts) |
| The import’s file line and bulk_change, once for each module sheet the file has whose module is off (today the Metric library’s Metrics sheet) | “{Module} is off in {workspace}, so the {sheet} sheet was not read.” | `moduleOffLine` (src/domain/sheets.ts) |
| Workspace → Features, after a switch is turned off (a message with Undo) | “{Module} is off in {workspace}. Nothing it saved is lost.” | `src/screens/Workspace.tsx` |
| Workspace → Features, after a switch is turned on (a message with Undo) | “{Module} is on in {workspace}.” | `src/screens/Workspace.tsx` |
| Workspace → Features, a module whose needs are off (under its name) | “Off until {the modules it needs} is on.” | `src/screens/Workspace.tsx` |

The import says once, in its file line, what it didn’t read because a module is off: today Reviews’ sheet and column, and the Metric library’s Metrics sheet (the two rows above). The file line’s “Not read: …” names every other sheet it didn’t read. A module whose records are not in the spreadsheet format (AI access’s tokens, Feedback’s inbox) has nothing for the import to say.

## The AI tools’ server and its door

One endpoint (Faro: `/api/mcp`) answering JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP POST, the Model Context Protocol’s tools: the core’s own tools and every installed module’s (90 today, 37 of them a module’s). Every tool and its inputs is in [the AI tools](../core/tools.md). Stage 3 builds the server with the core’s tools; AI access (its stage) adds making and revoking tokens and the switch that shuts the door.

### Who is asking

- A personal token, `gk_` and 40 letters or digits, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or `?token=` for an assistant that only takes an address). The server keeps only its SHA-256 hash, looks the token up by it, and acts as its person in its workspace; every save is logged as that person, marked “via MCP”.
- Each request loads the workspace afresh, its `modulesOff` included. A request the door let through moves the token’s last use.
- Making and revoking tokens is AI access’s (stage 4), so stage 3 has no screen that makes one. To test the server in stage 3, a build stores a token record itself (its hash, its person and workspace, no revoked date) and sends the token: what the door does with it is the same as with one AI access made.

| When | HTTP status | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| Not a POST (and not `?check` or `?picture=`) | 405, `Allow: GET, POST, OPTIONS` | error -32001 “This MCP server answers POST requests only (no event stream).” |
| No token (`Authorization: Bearer gk_…`, or `?token=` for an assistant that only takes an address) | 401, `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` | error -32001 “Add your personal token: Authorization: Bearer gk_… An admin makes one under Workspace → Access → MCP access.” |
| A token that isn’t live (unknown, or revoked); it is looked up by its SHA-256 hash | 401, `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"` | error -32001 “That token isn’t valid or has been revoked. Ask an admin for a new one.” |
| AI access switched off in the token’s workspace: each message but `initialize`, `tools/list` and notifications | 200 (the reply to each message) | error -32001 “AI access is switched off in {workspace}. An admin can switch it on in Faro, under Workspace, Features.”; the token’s last use doesn’t move |
| A body that isn’t JSON | 400 | error -32700 “Parse error” |
| The token’s person has left or been removed | 500 | error -32603 “The person this token belongs to is no longer in the workspace.” |

`GET ?check` answers without a token, saying only what works (`{ ok, database, pictures, problems }`), 200 when ok and 503 otherwise.

### The methods

| Method | Answer |
|---|---|
| `initialize` | `protocolVersion` (the one asked for when it is one of `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26`, `2024-11-05`, else `2025-06-18`), `capabilities` (tools and prompts, neither `listChanged`), `serverInfo` (`name: goals`, `title: Faro`, `version: 1.0.0`) and `instructions`. |
| `ping` | `{}` |
| `tools/list` | Every tool, the core’s and every installed module’s, on or off: `name`, `title`, `description`, `inputSchema`, `annotations`. A switched-off module’s tools stay listed, so an assistant learns why a call refuses. |
| `tools/call` | `{ name, arguments }`: `{ content: [{ type: "text", text }, …images], structuredContent?, isError }`. An unknown name is error -32602 “Unknown tool: {name}”. |
| `prompts/list`, `prompts/get` | The server’s prompts (Feedback’s `review_inbox`); an unknown one is -32602 “Unknown prompt: {name}”. |
| a notification (no `id`), any `notifications/…` | No reply, except that `initialize`, `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, `prompts/get` and `tools/call` are answered even with no `id` (`id: null`); only `ping`, `notifications/…` and an unknown method go unanswered. A body with nothing to reply is answered 202 with no body. |
| anything else | error -32601 “Method not found: {method}”; a message that isn’t JSON-RPC 2.0 is -32600 “Invalid request”. |

- **Batches.** A body may be an array of messages: they run one at a time, in order, so a later call sees what an earlier one saved; the replies come back as an array, notifications left out.
- **A tool’s refusals** are a result with `isError: true` and the words in `text`, never a JSON-RPC error: a switched-off module’s tool, or a core tool asked for what one adds (the tool’s sentence, above), and a rule saying no, followed by who the token acts as (“This token acts as {name}, who isn’t an admin.”). A name with no tool is refused before any tool runs, as the JSON-RPC error -32602 “Unknown tool: {name}” (the methods, above).
- **Stale saves.** A save refused because someone else changed the same goal or review since the request loaded it runs the tool again on the latest, up to twice more; a re-run that saved starts its text “Someone else changed this a moment ago, so it ran again on the latest and was saved as follows. If you checked it first with a dry run, check what it says now.”, and one refused every time says “Someone else changed this a moment ago, so it wasn’t saved. Read it again (get_goal or get_review) and try again.”
- **Dry runs.** Every tool that writes and takes `dry_run` (9 today: `post_check_in`, `update_goal`, `make_goal_active`, `make_goal_proposed`, `create_goal`, `set_plan_numbers`, `start_next_cycle`, `undo_import`, `set_goal_fields`) checks and says what it would save with `dry_run: true`, and saves nothing; `bulk_change` previews unless given `apply`. A dry run follows the same rules and refusals as the save.

## What proves it (stage 3’s exit criterion for the platform)

With one example module (Faro’s conformance uses `example`: a menu row “Example” in the `lookup` group at `/example`, as in `navigation.csv`) that adds a route, a menu row, a part in a place, a Help article, an action and an AI tool:

1. With it on, each shows where this page says, and its action and tool run.
2. Switched off by an admin on Workspace → Features: its row, page, part, article and Workspace section are gone; its address is Page not found with “{Module} is switched off in {workspace}. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, Features.”; its action is refused with the action’s sentence; its tool is still listed and answers with the tool’s sentence; the change is in the log; nothing it saved is deleted, and switching it back on brings everything back.
3. Someone who isn’t an admin can’t switch it (the rule’s words), and a module that needs it goes off with it. No installed module has `needs` today (the table above), so prove this half with a second example module whose `needs` names the first: switching the first off switches both off, logs “, and with it {the second}”, and Features says “Off until {the first} is on.” under the second.
4. Built without the module at all, the core runs every core journey, the server answers the core’s tools, and Features shows no switch for it.
5. The server answers `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list` and a batch as above, refuses a missing or revoked token with 401 and its words, and a write with `dry_run: true` saves nothing.
